title: Probation Success Accelerator — 42Day Twin-Track Evaluation
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, operational playbook for People Ops + hiring managers to run a concentrated 42-day probation accelerator for mid-level ICs (L3-L4) who need structured, high-touch ramping. The goal is to create a predictable twin-track evaluation that separates ramp fidelity (skill acquisition & deliveries) from autonomy signals (ownership, escalation handling, cross-team collaboration).

Why 42 days?
- 6-week window gives enough signal for competency without long probation tail.
- Aligns with common sprint cycles and gives time for 3 structured checkpoints.

Scope and when to use this doc:
- Use when a hire needs an explicit early acceleration plan (post-offer / day 0) or when probation progress is marginal at day 30 and manager+People Ops want a focused remediation/validation sprint.
- Not for interns or executive hires (use standard offer/probation channels).

High-level flow (owner responsibilities):
- People Ops: set up the program, templates, meeting cadence, collect artifacts, run weekly calibration with Hiring Manager and Buddy.
- Hiring Manager: define twin-track deliverables, assign buddy rotations, provide weekly feedback, make final recommendation.
- Buddy: daily 1:1 support first 14 days, then peer-check-ins, shadowing notes.

Twin-track evaluation model (explicit separation of signals):
1) Ramp Track (60% of final pass mark):
  - Deliverables: 2 small production-facing tasks (one cross-functional) + docs updated + 1 code review sign-off responsibility.
  - Evidence: PRs merged, feature flag rollout notes, short demo recording, updated runbook.
  - Scoring: objective checkboxes (done / partial / not started) + owner comments.

2) Autonomy Track (40% of final pass mark):
  - Signals: incident triage participation, owning a single low-risk bug fix end-to-end, async communication quality, meeting facilitation for 1 team sync.
  - Evidence: pager duty runbook interaction, postmortem contribution, peer feedback snippets.
  - Scoring: behavioral rubric (1–5 scale) across four dimensions (Ownership, Communication, Judgment, Collaboration).

42-day schedule (minimal calendar):
- Day 0–7: onboarding sprint 
  - Access checklist (see below) completed by Day 2.
  - Buddy paired; daily 15–30m for 7 days.
  - Ramp Track: start first micro-project.
  - Autonomy Track: shadow incident runbook and sit-in on two triage calls.
- Day 8–21: delivery & feedback loop
  - Weekly 30m sync (Manager + hire) at end of each week.
  - People Ops check-in at Day 14 (pulse survey + 1:1 calibration).
  - Midpoint review (Day 21): informal readout, update rubric scores.
- Day 22–35: stretch & cross-pollinate
  - Assign cross-team microtask; schedule peer rotations (48–72 hour shadow).
  - Encourage candidate to lead a 15-minute team demo by Day 28.
- Day 36–42: consolidation & final evaluation
  - Final evidence bundle due Day 40 (links to PRs, recordings, runbooks, peer feedback).
  - Formal 1-hour evaluation meeting Day 41 (People Ops + Manager + Buddy + 1 peer).
  - Decision communicated Day 42 with written notes and next steps.

Access & Day 0 checklist (manager / IT / security):
- Code repo access: repo A (read/write), repo B (read).
- CI/CD access + deploy preview token assigned.
- Slack + team channels + calendar invites populated.
- Cloud console IAM role created (least privilege) and logged.
- Internal wiki/runbooks: edit rights to team docs.
- Pager/test incident access: read-only to start; escalation path documented.

Deliverable templates (links in linked_artifacts):
- Micro-project brief (one page): context, acceptance criteria, rough estimate, owner, reviewers.
- Evidence bundle checklist: PR links, demo recording, runbook diff, peer feedback snippets.
- Final recommendation form: pass / pass-with-development-plan / extend-probation (21 days) / no-pass.

Interview & evaluation rubrics (used for calibration and final scoring):
A. Competency anchors (behavioral, 1–5 scale):
  - Ownership: 1 (avoids responsibility) to 5 (proactively reduces risk across team).
  - Communication: 1 (unclear or noisy async) to 5 (clear, structured, concise updates).
  - Judgment: 1 (ignores context) to 5 (tradeoff-aware, escalates appropriately).
  - Collaboration: 1 (siloed) to 5 (actively pulls others, gives helpful reviews).

B. Technical tradecraft checklist (pass/fail-ish signals):
  - Can produce a deployable PR with tests and CI passing.
  - Demonstrates code review hygiene (responds to feedback, iterates).
  - Understands basic perf/debug tools used by team.

Calibration probes (quick manager prompts to collect evidence):
  - "Show me the smallest change that would make this feature ship faster — what tradeoffs?"
  - "Walk me through how you’d signal an outage and who you’d loop in."
  - "Give an example of a time you changed a team decision based on data or feedback."

Scoring model (example weights):
  - Ramp Track: 0.6 * (deliverable completion ratio)
  - Autonomy Track: 0.4 * (average competency anchor score / 5)
  - Thresholds: >=0.72 = pass; 0.60–0.71 = pass-with-development-plan; 0.45–0.59 = extend probation 21 days; <0.45 = no-pass.

Feedback cadence & templates:
- Weekly short-form feedback (template): 3 bullets — What went well, What to improve, Blockers & help needed.
- Midpoint readout (15 min) — candidate demo + manager 5-min score summary.
- Final evaluation (1 hr) — present evidence bundle, blinded peer feedback readout, collective score, decision.

Buddy rotation guidelines:
- 0–14 days: daily 15–30m.
- 15–28 days: alternate days for pair programming / shadow sessions.
- 29–42 days: weekly check-ins + rapid async notes.
- Buddy should provide 3 short bullet observations by Day 21 and a narrative by Day 40.

Remediation & escalation playbook:
- If any red flags (security, major non-delivery, conduct) appear, pause the standard 42-day flow and escalate to People Ops with immediate triage (24 hours).
- For technical shortfalls: propose a 21-day remediation focused only on the weakest competency with 2 clearly scoped tasks and twice-weekly check-ins.

Example final recommendation note (template):
- Hire: Maria Gomez
- Role: Platform Engineer L3
- Summary: Strong ramp on code deliverables (2/2 micro-projects shipped), needs clearer async updates during triage; recommended pass-with-development-plan.
- Action items: 30-day mentor pairing for async comms, 1 monthly triage facilitation slot.

Practical notes / tips from pilots:
- Keep evidence minimal and link-only; reviewers won’t read long prose.
- Use short video demos (2–4 minutes) — higher signal than long writeups.
- Separate perception from objective signals — e.g., a missed internal meeting is lower weight than a failed production rollout.

Open questions / TODOs for People Ops team:
- Align final recommendation wording with legal for locales with strict probation laws.
- Add localized access template for on-prem/private deployments (security team).
- Create a small Notion/Confluence panel to store blinded peer feedback snippets for easier calibration.

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Day 0 access checklist completed
- [ ] Buddy assigned (name + calendar invites)
- [ ] Micro-project briefs created (2)
- [ ] Weekly feedback template scheduled
- [ ] Midpoint check-in scheduled Day 21
- [ ] Evidence bundle deadline Day 40 set
- [ ] Final evaluation meeting Day 41 scheduled

If you want a copy of the evaluation spreadsheet or the short video demo template, ping me (Marina) or see linked_artifacts.

Notes to self (rough):
- Pilot run with eng-platform Q4; measure: % pass, average time to productive PR, manager satisfaction.
- Consider a light-weight automation: a small form that collects PR links + peers and auto-aggregates scores into the final decision sheet.
